title: Sandalwood and vanilla solid perfume
subtitle: A pocket-sized anhydrous perfume balm
excerpt: A solid perfume balm of beeswax, jojoba oil, sandalwood, and vanilla fragrance oil poured into a small tin. Warm, woody, and sweet. Apply with a fingertip. Makes one 15 ml tin.
sourceNotes: Beeswax-to-oil ratio for solid perfume: standard formulation reference (30-40% beeswax to carrier oil for a firm-but-smooth texture). Fragrance oil loading in anhydrous products: IFRA guidelines for candle-grade fragrance oils; general cosmetic formulation literature for leave-on products.

recipe.batchNotes: Pours into four 15 ml tins at the same scale; multiply ingredients by four.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Sets in two hours. Store in the tin until ready to use.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps one year in a sealed tin in a cool, dark cupboard. Discard if the surface develops white spots or the balm smells sharp rather than sweet and woody. The jojoba oil base is stable for two to three years; the fragrance note fades after about a year.

glossaryTerms.definition: An anhydrous, wax-based perfume that melts on contact with skin warmth and releases its fragrance as the carrier oil spreads. The wax keeps the fragrance concentrated without a liquid solvent; the carrier oil prolongs the scent on skin.

content.text: is a beeswax-and-oil balm that carries the fragrance in a concentrated, portable form. This one blends sandalwood essential oil with vanilla fragrance oil for a warm, skin-forward base note that lasts through the day. Apply a small amount with a clean fingertip to pulse points.
Apply a patch test on the inside of the forearm before the first use and leave for 24 hours.

items.prepNote: cosmetic grade; 33% of the formula by weight
53% of formula; stable carrier that carries scent on skin
vanilla fragrance oil; IFRA-rated for leave-on skin use; check the supplier's skin-safe guidance

content.text: Melt the beeswax and jojoba oil together in a heatproof bowl over a saucepan of barely simmering water. Stir until the beeswax is fully liquid. Remove from the heat and let cool to 55°C.
Add the cedarwood essential oil and the vanilla fragrance oil. Stir once. Pour immediately into the tin before the beeswax sets. The beeswax cools quickly once off the heat.
Leave the tin on a flat surface for two hours. Do not move it while the surface is setting or the top will wrinkle. Once the perfume is firm and opaque, press on the lid.
Keeps one year in a sealed tin in a cool, dark cupboard. Discard if the surface develops white spots or the balm smells sharp rather than sweet and woody.
